name: Vachellia

project_scope.note: Comparison framework only. Species learner admission/range/canonical installation remain independent.
project_scope.canonical_status: Both species now installed with exact-species provisional licensed photos; strict native-range statuses remain UNRESOLVED.

genus_diagnostics.shared: Woody thorny mimosoid legumes with alternate bipinnate leaves, paired straight stipular spines at nodes, globose yellow flower heads, and legume fruits.
genus_diagnostics.look_here_first: Confirm paired straight stipular spines at a leaf node, then confirm a bipinnate leaf and a globose yellow flower head. Once Vachellia is established, move to mature pod shape and leaflet/pinna counts for the species split.
genus_diagnostics.caution: Flower color and the generic yellow puffball gestalt are not enough; several mimosoid legumes can look similar. Use node armature, leaf architecture, and mature fruit together.

separating_characters.mature_pod: Long, narrow pod; commonly about 3–6 mm wide and up to about 12 cm long.
separating_characters.pinnae_leaflets: Typically about 3–9 pairs of pinnae, each with roughly 4–16 pairs of small leaflets; project lesson should treat counts as supporting ranges, not a single-character key.
separating_characters.armature: Paired straight pale/white stipular spines are conspicuous on younger stems.
separating_characters.habit_context: Usually shrub to small tree; drought/cold deciduous behavior can make winter twig armature especially useful.

species_comparison.learner_shortcut: Narrow pod + relatively fewer leaflets per pinna + conspicuous pale paired spines supports V. constricta.

separating_characters.mature_pod: Distinctly thicker, hard, plump to subcylindrical pod rather than the very narrow pod of V. constricta.
separating_characters.pinnae_leaflets: Commonly about 2–6 pairs of pinnae with about 10–25 pairs of narrow leaflets per pinna in regional descriptions.
separating_characters.armature: Also has paired straight stipular spines, so spines establish the genus pattern but do not by themselves separate it from V. constricta.
separating_characters.flowers: Globose yellow heads are notably fragrant; fragrance is supporting only, not the primary diagnostic.

species_comparison.learner_shortcut: Thick hard pod + denser leaflet complement supports V. farnesiana.

comparison_matrix.farnesiana: much thicker, hard/plump to subcylindrical legume

comparison_matrix.constricta: generally fewer leaflet pairs per pinna
comparison_matrix.farnesiana: generally more numerous leaflet pairs per pinna

comparison_matrix.weight: strong genus cue; weak species separator

lookalikes.group: other mimosoid Fabaceae in the source pool
lookalikes.tie_breaker: Do not key from yellow puffball flowers alone. Verify paired stipular spines at the node, then leaf architecture and mature pod.
Use armature position/type and mature fruit plus current accepted genus placement; hand off uncertain generic boundaries rather than guessing from foliage.

overlap_cautions: Both species can be thorny shrubs/small trees with fine bipinnate foliage and yellow globose heads.
Pinna and leaflet counts overlap and should not be used alone.
Young or absent fruit can make the species split substantially harder; mark such observations as needing reproductive confirmation rather than forcing an ID.
Do not reopen native-range decisions in this lesson. The Master Plant Pool currently carries V. constricta and V. farnesiana as source-pool taxa with their own independent review states.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: Show the genus-level armature exactly where it attaches; include petiole base and node.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.role: whole bipinnate leaf, flat and in focus
diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: Count pinnae and compare leaflet density between species.
Primary species split: very narrow V. constricta pod versus thick hard V. farnesiana pod.
Connect the yellow globose head to the correct thorny bipinnate plant rather than using a detached flower portrait.
Show paired spine architecture when foliage is absent, especially useful for V. constricta.

media_handoff.priority: Use project/user/Joey media if an exact-species frame clearly shows node armature, leaf architecture, or mature fruit. Do not acquire generic gallery photos in this lane.
media_handoff.desired_visual_lock: One same-scale mature-pod comparison plus one labeled node/spine comparison would provide the highest learner value.

diagnostic_review_handoff: If a future diagnostic reviewer finds local material with pod dimensions or leaflet counts outside these regional ranges, refine the matrix using Texas herbarium/flora evidence rather than forcing the count ranges.
Confirm any source-pool records using older Acacia names map cleanly to the current Vachellia concepts before adding aliases to species cards.

sources.role: taxonomy, growth form, paired spines, regional ecology

look_here_first: Inspect a twig node for a PAIR of STRAIGHT stipular spines and examine its bipinnate leaves. Both have golden spherical flower heads; compare MATURE pods: whitethorn is slender and constricted, huisache thick and dark.

shared_traits: Thorny small trees or shrubs with alternate bipinnate leaves.
Usually paired STRAIGHT stipular spines at the leaf node, unlike recurved prickles of Senegalia.
Golden ball-shaped heads of very small flowers with conspicuous stamens.
Pod shape and size are better species clues than flower color alone.
priority: Find thorn origin precisely at the stem NODE
Count primary pinnae and paired tiny leaflets on a complete compound leaf
Find MATURE fruits: slender constricted whitethorn pods versus thicker dark husk-like huisache pods
Photograph yellow flower head with nearby leaf + thorn
study_strategy.warning: Paired thorns can vary, and leaf/pinna counts overlap. Do not identify to species from one isolated gold flower head.

quick_key.if: paired straight spines + gold heads + very slender constricted, elongated pod
paired straight spines + gold heads + stout dark brown/black swollen pod
elongate pale flower spikes + long straw pods
